profile.reading:
DataBank's Plano campus sits at 8375 Dominion Parkway, Plano, Texas, in the Legacy Park business district of the Dallas-Fort Worth metro. DataBank operates two co-located facilities at this one address, DFW3 and DFW8; the company's public materials do not clearly disambiguate which physical structure carries which code at the shared address, so this OSM-mapped building is recorded under the shared campus address rather than assigned definitively to one code. DataBank's current directory page states DFW3 at 72,230 square feet of IT space and 12 megawatts of critical IT load, and DFW8 at 126,000 square feet and 40 megawatts, for a combined campus total near 198,000 square feet; earlier 2021 press releases describe DFW3 alone at up to 40 megawatts of total power capacity across an expanded 144,000 square feet of expandable space, figures that do not fully reconcile with the current directory page's 12-megawatt DFW3 listing, a discrepancy this profile notes rather than resolves. A July 2021 press release describes a Data Hall 3 expansion (12,000 additional square feet, 1.5 additional megawatts) and a December 2021 release describes Data Halls 5 and 6 (22,000 additional square feet, 3 additional megawatts), both targeting completion in 2022, and both citing Uptime Institute Tier III certification. DataBank names Oncor as the power utility for this campus, describing "dual feeds from Oncor." The Plano campus is described as interconnected with DataBank's DFW1 and DFW2 Dallas-area facilities, and carries FedRAMP/FISMA, HIPAA HITECH, SOC 1/2, SSAE 18, and PCI DSS compliance certifications, with 47 onsite network carriers per DataBank's directory page.

Plano's Legacy Park business district has grown into one of the largest suburban corporate campus concentrations in Texas, anchoring major headquarters relocations from Toyota, JPMorgan Chase, and other large employers over the past decade, a dynamic that has helped drive enterprise colocation demand for DataBank's Plano campus alongside its role serving DataBank's broader interconnected DFW facility network. Collin County, where Plano sits, has separately courted large-scale technology and data infrastructure investment as part of its own economic-development strategy distinct from Dallas County's downtown-focused approach.

profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-03, batch 97 (DataBank): operator own dedicated page confirmed the existing address and added IT capacity and sqft, research_status upgraded from exhausted to complete.

[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to DataBank. DataBank Ltd. was established in 2005 in a historic former Federal Reserve Bank building in downtown Dallas, Texas, that had been converted to a data center in 1999, per DataBank own corporate history page fetched this session. DataBank was acquired in July 2016 by a group of investors led by DigitalBridge, per that same page. DataBank own history page also lists a series of acquisitions expanding its footprint, three Salt Lake City area data centers from C7 Data Centers plus facilities in Cleveland and Pittsburgh from 365 Data Centers in January 2017, Lightbound, an Indianapolis based provider, in December 2018, United States and United Kingdom data center assets from zColo in December 2020, and four Houston area data centers from CyrusOne for 670 million dollars in January 2022. A trade press article fetched this session, from pe-insights.com, reports that DigitalBridge agreed to sell a 27 percent fully diluted equity stake in DataBank to Swiss Life Asset Management and EDF Invest for about 1.2 billion dollars, expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2022, reducing DigitalBridge own stake to about 15.5 percent and yielding DigitalBridge about 230 million dollars in cash proceeds. DataBank own history page states the company now operates more than 65 data centers across more than 27 markets. The operator own dedicated page for this facility, Plano, designated DFW3, fetched this session, confirms the address already on file, 8375 Dominion Pkwy, Plano, TX 75024, and states 12 MW of critical IT load and 72,230 IT square feet.

reading.body:
A 12 MW data center in Plano, Texas can support between 300 and 1,200 racks depending on whether it runs AI training workloads at 40 kW per rack or standard colocation at 10 kW per rack, but the operator does not publish which power density it targets.

The gap between these two scenarios matters because it determines whether this facility serves compute-intensive AI training, which requires tight thermal and electrical management, or general-purpose hosting, which permits looser configurations. DataBank publishes only the megawatt figure and technical square footage. No power density ceiling, no workload type, and no thermal design specification appear on the facility page. This opacity is common across the industry and prevents external assessment of how much AI-capable compute actually sits behind a stated megawatt figure.

DataBank's FedRAMP certification qualifies it to host U.S. federal government workloads under that program's security rules. It is the only certification listed. No SOC 2, PCI DSS, or other standards appear on the specification sheet. FedRAMP is specific to federal compliance and does not signal preparedness for commercial AI training workloads or enterprise security requirements beyond government scope.

Among DataBank facilities in the Plano area that publish capacity figures, this campus ranks tenth by stated IT megawatts. Thirteen facilities in that group together publish 389 MW. This ranking reflects only disclosed capacity on pages the site has read, not total installed infrastructure or future expansion plans DataBank may not have made public.
